# Highlight comparison fixtures

This directory contains independently authored source specimens, language-independent diff pairs, exact case ranges and provenance. The source is inert input data: collectors and regression tests may read or parse it, but must not execute source files. These files declare no expected parser categories, token scopes, colors or font attributes. `manifest.json` uses schema 1; ranges are one-based and inclusive, and cases may overlap when the same text belongs to multiple contexts.

## Coverage and deliberate limits

The corpus samples intact positive syntax contexts; it is not exhaustive, a compiler replacement or a language conformance suite. The common feature families are comments/documentation, quoted and multiline strings/escapes, numeric forms, names/declarations/types, operators/delimiters, control flow, modern language-specific syntax and embedded-language boundaries where applicable.

| Specimen | Language/version | Coverage emphasis | Not represented here |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `markdown-commonmark-0.31.2.md` | CommonMark 0.31.2 | headings, paragraphs, inline/reference links, image, simple and multiple-backtick code spans, entities, indented/fenced code, lists, quotes and raw HTML | invalid delimiter fragments, exhaustive block precedence |
| `markdown-gfm-0.29-gfm.md` | GFM 0.29-gfm (CommonMark 0.29-derived) | tables, task lists, strikethrough, CommonMark angle-bracket autolinks and the GFM extended bare-URL autolink | the full CommonMark/GFM conformance suites |
| `json-core.json` | RFC 8259 JSON | objects/arrays, strings/escapes/Unicode, numbers, booleans and null | comments, trailing commas, duplicate keys, JSON5 |
| `yaml-core.yaml` | YAML 1.2.2 Core schema | flow/block collections, comments, aliases, quoted/plain/block scalars, all three chomping modes, standard tags, directives and document markers | duplicate keys, YAML 1.1 implicit typing/merges, custom object constructors and application-specific tag schemes |
| `go-core.go` | Go 1.27; syntax floor Go 1.24 | complete package entry point, generic declarations and aliases, constraints, range integer and iterator function, receiver method, directed channels, `defer`/`select`, literals, comments, operators and control flow | third-party packages, generated files, executable tests and Go 1.27-only syntax beyond this 1.24 floor |
| `cpp-core.cpp` | C++23 | preprocessing, standard headers, literals, concepts/requires, templates, constexpr, lambda, attributes, structured binding and operators | modules/BMI setup, compiler extensions and C++26 proposals |
| `rust-core.rs` | Rust edition 2024 | lifetimes, borrowing, patterns, traits/generics/impl, macros, async/await with `Result` propagation and `let-else`, raw/byte strings, raw identifier and explicit unsafe block | external crates, executable tests, edition-2024-only migration hazards not useful as positive syntax |
| `typescript-core.ts` | TypeScript 5.9 | line/block comments with keyword-looking string text, enums/namespaces/parameter properties, decorators, interfaces, generic/mapped/conditional/template types, `satisfies`, `as const` and type-only import | JSX/TSX, semantic type-checking of the inert external type import, exhaustive compiler options |
| `javascript-core.js` | ECMAScript 2024 module syntax | line/block comments with keyword-looking string text, import/export, decimal/radix/BigInt literals, regex versus division, private fields, destructuring/spread, async generators, arrow function with `await`, and optional/nullish operators | CommonJS, runtime host-API behavior and syntax adopted after the 2024 snapshot |
| `bash-core.sh` | GNU Bash 5.3 | comments, quoting/parameter/arithmetic/brace/pathname expansion, indexed/associative arrays, functions, case, loops, regex tests, pipes, output/input redirections, here-documents/strings and process substitution | execution, interactive/job-control behavior, platform utilities and non-Bash POSIX-shell compatibility |
| `html-core.html` | WHATWG HTML Living Standard | complete document, metadata, comments/entities, semantic elements, attributes, CSS and JavaScript embedding | browser behavior, accessibility conformance, fetched resources and full HTML conformance |
| `css-core.css` | CSS Syntax Level 3 plus named module snapshots | selectors, escapes/strings/numbers/units/colors, custom properties, `var()`, `calc()`, layers, media/supports, keyframes and nesting | property-value conformance, layout/paint/browser behavior, fetches and exhaustive selector/property coverage |
| `python-core.py`, `python-3.14.py`, `python-projection.py` | Python 3.14 | existing Python lexical/modern syntax and terminal projection controls | see the Python-specific notes below |
| `diff/` | language-independent text | original old/new text, context/add/remove/replace, blank rows and coordinates | application-specific tool records, colors and terminal grids |

The JavaScript and HTML specimens are syntax/data inputs only; HTML's embedded CSS and JavaScript are never evaluated, and their fragment links do not cause network access. The YAML fixture explicitly enables YAML 1.2 and the Core schema; its simple `yes` remains a string, `<<` is not treated as an implicit merge key, and duplicate mapping keys are rejected by the semantic regression. No new language is claimed capturable by OpenCode: its current source adapter still accepts only `.py`. New languages have no native capture or theme-sweep acceptance. The existing Python/diff pilot evidence remains specific to those original inputs.

## Markdown dialects and license inventory

Markdown files deliberately declare distinct parser targets. The CommonMark specimen targets the official 0.31.2 specification. The GFM specimen targets GitHub Flavored Markdown 0.29-gfm, whose base is CommonMark 0.29; it must not be relabelled as CommonMark 0.31.2. Its bare-URL token witness exercises GFM's extended autolink, unlike the CommonMark angle-bracket form. The existing `marked` checks are token witnesses for these samples, not a CommonMark or GFM conformance oracle.

All non-Python specimens are original examples written for this corpus. The official specifications and manuals linked below informed syntax/version inventories only. No normative example, language implementation regression test, grammar sample, expected scope, or color assertion was copied or adapted. The sources are linked for verifiability; their licenses do not transfer to these independently authored files.

## Source data and parse-only validation

Specimens are read as bytes, never imported as executable modules. The root `tsconfig.json` excludes only `tests/fixtures/highlight-compare` from the project program: enums, namespaces and parameter properties are valid TypeScript input even though the extension's runtime code must remain `erasableSyntaxOnly`. The regression checks parse the declared TypeScript inputs separately and verify that real source/tests remain in the project program and that the test catalogue does not execute fixture data.

Use the [prepared, memory-contained test commands](../../../docs/testing.md#requirements-and-commands) for `harness/highlight-compare/fixtures.test.mjs` and `harness/highlight-compare/language-semantics.test.mjs`. They use the selected graph's TypeScript, `marked` and YAML parser references. The CSS transformer, esbuild, is an explicitly declared development tool installed into both minimum and alternate Pi graphs, independent of Pi's transitive dependencies; JavaScript uses Node's module `--check` mode. YAML parsing explicitly selects 1.2 Core, unique mapping keys and no implicit merge extension. Markdown token witnesses and CSS parsing with no warnings are not conformance certificates. HTML's error-recovering tokenization and embedded-language syntax need separate authoring checks, not a browser or an HTML4 parser substituted for HTML5 conformance.

Host compiler checks are authoring tools, not additional prerequisites for ordinary Node tests: `gofmt -l -e` checks Go parsing without writing source; C++ uses `-std=c++23 -pedantic-errors -fsyntax-only`; Rust uses `--edition=2024 --crate-type=lib --crate-name highlight_compare --emit=metadata` with an explicit untracked output; Bash uses `--noprofile --norc -n`. Keep compiler/cache outputs outside source and use the testing guide's isolated environment and memory scope. Never run a compiled Go/C++/Rust output, source the Bash file, evaluate the JavaScript, or fetch Markdown/HTML links to validate these specimens. `gofmt -l` may list a syntactically valid file that it would reformat; that list alone is not a syntax error. Positive parsing/compilation does not prove runtime correctness.

## Python source and coverage

Each Python entry names its target language version, source file and explicit one-based inclusive case ranges. Case ranges may overlap when one construct appears inside another; the declared features, not source-line counts, describe intended coverage.

All three Python files target the Python 3.14 parser. `python-core.py` contains positive syntax available by Python 3.13, including PEP 695 generic declarations and PEP 696 default type parameters. `python-3.14.py` isolates syntax added in 3.14: template strings and an `except` clause with unparenthesized multiple exception types. The 3.14-only additions are intentionally retained even if a comparison highlighter does not recognize them. Free names and inert-looking function bodies are deliberate: comparison fixtures are parsed as data and must never be executed.

The Python files are independently authored. No upstream example, excerpt, highlighting scope assertion or expected color was copied or adapted. The official references below informed the construct inventory and version boundaries only.

`python-projection.py` supplies independently authored terminal-mapping controls: actual tab-indented source, a wide identifier, a combining character and one oversized unbroken fragment. A narrow-terminal control must preserve its original source positions instead of comparing screen columns.

## Diff pairs

The `.txt` pairs contain plain text with LF line endings, independent of programming-language syntax. `roleSamples` in the manifest gives exact source-coordinate/text witnesses for context, added and removed rows; they are not a complete serialized patch or color expectation. The mixed pair has changed content, replacement, context, a removed blank row and multi-digit line numbers. The second pair has an empty old side and added blank/content rows. Consumers derive their own native saved-tool representation from a neutral standard patch with three context rows. Validate the complete before/after transformation, including unchanged file margins outside those hunks; require every declared hunk row and structural witness on screen. This avoids confusing Pi's normal three-row context window with missing syntax data. No application-specific wire format belongs in these fixture files.

`native-layout-inputs.mjs` supplies independently authored LF text pairs and neutral role witnesses for layout-boundary regressions and opt-in native checks: an empty old pane, a context-only pane opposite twelve insertions, nine removed rows paired with one added row, and nine fully replaced file rows producing eighteen unified diff rows. The same pairs also drive derived no-final-LF, context-marker and symmetric empty-side controls. These are not additional default manifest comparison specimens and contain no expected styles, terminal grids or application-specific tool records.

## Python provenance and licensing

The Python feature inventory and version boundaries were checked against the official CPython **v3.14.0**, commit `ebf955df7a89ed0c7968f79faec1de49f61ed7cb`, language reference and grammar:

- [CPython v3.14.0 PEG grammar](https://github.com/python/cpython/blob/ebf955df7a89ed0c7968f79faec1de49f61ed7cb/Grammar/python.gram)
- [Lexical analysis](https://github.com/python/cpython/blob/ebf955df7a89ed0c7968f79faec1de49f61ed7cb/Doc/reference/lexical_analysis.rst): comments, identifiers/soft keywords, literals and escapes, f-strings/t-strings, numeric literals, operators and delimiters
- [Compound statements](https://github.com/python/cpython/blob/ebf955df7a89ed0c7968f79faec1de49f61ed7cb/Doc/reference/compound_stmts.rst): flow control, exception and exception-group handlers, matching patterns, functions/classes, coroutines and type-parameter lists
- [Expressions](https://github.com/python/cpython/blob/ebf955df7a89ed0c7968f79faec1de49f61ed7cb/Doc/reference/expressions.rst): displays/comprehensions, calls, subscriptions/slices, operators, assignment expressions, lambdas and generators
- [Simple statements](https://github.com/python/cpython/blob/ebf955df7a89ed0c7968f79faec1de49f61ed7cb/Doc/reference/simple_stmts.rst): assignment/unpacking, imports, `yield`, `raise` and the `type` statement
- [CPython v3.14.0 license](https://github.com/python/cpython/blob/ebf955df7a89ed0c7968f79faec1de49f61ed7cb/LICENSE) and [documentation license](https://github.com/python/cpython/blob/ebf955df7a89ed0c7968f79faec1de49f61ed7cb/Doc/license.rst): Python and its documentation are under PSF License Version 2; code examples in the documentation are dual-licensed under PSF License Version 2 and Zero-Clause BSD. No documentation code example was reused.
- [PEP 750](https://peps.python.org/pep-0750/) specifies template strings; [PEP 758](https://peps.python.org/pep-0758/) specifies optional parentheses for multiple exception types. The pinned language reference records both as Python 3.14 additions. PEP 696's default type parameters are covered by the pinned reference's version note that support was added in Python 3.13.

The [Learn X in Y Minutes Python page](https://github.com/adambard/learnxinyminutes-docs/blob/master/python.md) was screened as a possible breadth reference but not used as fixture text; its [repository README](https://github.com/adambard/learnxinyminutes-docs/blob/master/README.md) identifies the documentation license as CC BY-SA 3.0. The [Sublime Text Python syntax-test file](https://github.com/sublimehq/Packages/blob/master/Python/tests/syntax_test_python.py) was not used; its tests encode that grammar's scopes and the [repository license](https://github.com/sublimehq/Packages/blob/master/LICENSE) notes file-specific exceptions. Neither source's wording, test cases, scope assertions or color expectations appear here.

These fixtures assert no product-specific token categories, foregrounds, backgrounds or font attributes. Python syntax validation uses the declared Python 3.14 parser and must not execute fixture code. `syntaxBaseline` describes the oldest language syntax used by the core specimen; it is not a claim that a separate Python 3.13 interpreter was tested. These compact files are not exhaustive: intentionally invalid/incomplete code, interactive-only syntax and exhaustive operator/prefix combinations are not covered.
